domain: Energy Policy / Climate Mitigation / Technology Governance
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested role of nuclear power expansion in climate decarbonization strategy. The dispute centers on whether nuclear is a necessary complement to renewables for reliable baseload power or a capital-intensive distraction that delays faster renewable deployment. The kernel is the climate-mitigation imperative itself; parties read it through incompatible frameworks that emit structurally different constraints.

key_entities: Nuclear power industry (existing fleet + new reactor designs)
Climate mitigation imperative (Paris Agreement targets, net-zero commitments)
Grid reliability requirements (baseload vs intermittency management)
Capital allocation mechanisms (public subsidy, private investment, opportunity cost)
Waste disposal systems (geological repositories, interim storage)
key_tensions: Baseload reliability vs renewable intermittency (nuclear advocates vs renewable advocates)
Construction timeline vs deployment urgency (nuclear's 10-15 year build vs renewable's 2-3 year)
Centralized vs distributed generation (large reactors vs distributed renewables + storage)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The climate mitigation imperative — the shared commitment to rapid, deep decarbonization to avoid catastrophic warming
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Scientific consensus (IPCC) establishes the physical constraint; interpretive authority over what constitutes adequate response is contested between techno-optimist, risk-minimization, and systems-transition frameworks

readings.commitment: Mitigation requires maximizing all low-carbon sources; nuclear is necessary for reliable baseload
readings.expected_structural_delta: Nuclear enters beneficiary set (receives subsidy/support); fossil fuels are primary victim; constraint is technology-neutral carbon intensity

readings.commitment: Mitigation requires fastest deployment per dollar; nuclear's capital intensity and timeline make it net-harmful
readings.expected_structural_delta: Nuclear enters victim set (diverts capital from faster alternatives); renewables are beneficiaries; constraint is carbon-per-dollar-per-year

readings.commitment: Mitigation requires transforming energy systems toward decentralization and democratic control; nuclear perpetuates extractive centralization
readings.expected_structural_delta: Nuclear enters victim set (incompatible with democratic energy transition); distributed renewables are beneficiaries; constraint is governance structure not just carbon

axiom_contradictions.basis: Portfolio reading holds 'all low-carbon sources are complementary' as axiomatic; opportunity-cost reading holds 'capital scarcity makes nuclear and renewables substitutes' as axiomatic. No single framework can hold both: either capital is abundant enough for portfolio diversification (A) or scarce enough that nuclear crowds out renewables (B).

Portfolio reading treats governance structure as orthogonal to mitigation effectiveness; systems-transition reading treats centralized vs democratic control as constitutive of what counts as mitigation. No framework can hold both: either mitigation is technology-neutral (A) or governance structure is part of the climate problem (B).

axes.human_readable: Portfolio Optimization Reading (Nuclear as Necessary Baseload)
axes.structural_delta: Nuclear power is necessary complement to renewables for reliable low-carbon baseload
axes.primary_observable: Grid reliability metrics (capacity factor, dispatchability); carbon intensity per kWh
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; represents techno-optimist framework

axes.human_readable: Opportunity Cost Reading (Nuclear as Capital Diversion)
axes.structural_delta: Nuclear's capital intensity and construction timeline make it net-harmful to mitigation goals
axes.primary_observable: Deployment rate (GW/year); cost per ton CO2 avoided; construction timeline data
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; represents economic-efficiency framework

axes.human_readable: Systems Transition Reading (Nuclear as Governance Incompatibility)
axes.structural_delta: Nuclear perpetuates centralized extractive energy systems incompatible with democratic transition
axes.primary_observable: Ownership structure (state/corporate vs community); decision-making locus; waste burden distribution
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; represents political-ecology framework

axes.human_readable: Grid Intermittency Constraint (Physical Limits of Variable Renewables)
axes.structural_delta: Physical limits on grid stability with high penetration of variable renewables without storage or baseload
axes.primary_observable: Duck curve severity; curtailment rates; storage deployment vs need
axes.selection_reason: Independent mountain; upstream physical constraint that portfolio_optimization_reading invokes but opportunity_cost_reading contests as solvable via storage

axes.human_readable: Construction Timeline Lock-In (Nuclear's Decade-Scale Deployment Lag)
axes.structural_delta: Nuclear plants require 10-15 years from approval to operation vs 2-3 years for renewables
axes.primary_observable: Historical construction duration data; project completion rates
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: mountain feeding into opportunity_cost_reading but structurally captured by that reading's deployment-rate observable; independent generation would duplicate

axes.structural_delta: No operational geological repository for high-level waste; costs and risks externalized to future generations
axes.primary_observable: Repository status (operational, under construction, planned); interim storage capacity vs accumulation rate
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: feeds into systems_transition_reading's governance critique but lacks independent structural delta beyond that reading's waste-burden observable

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Nuclear's 10-15 year build time vs renewables' 2-3 years
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Mountain feeding into opportunity_cost_reading but structurally captured by that reading's deployment-rate observable; independent generation would duplicate constraint story

deferred_axes.structural_delta: No operational geological repository; intergenerational cost externalization
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Feeds into systems_transition_reading's governance critique but lacks independent structural delta beyond that reading's waste-burden distribution observable

omegas.description: If grid-scale storage costs drop 80%+ (plausible by 2035), does grid_intermittency_constraint collapse from mountain to rope? Portfolio_optimization_reading's baseload necessity claim depends on storage remaining expensive.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + grid_intermittency_constraint mountain validity

omegas.description: Small modular reactors (SMRs) claim 3-5 year construction timelines. If realized, does construction_timeline_lock_in mountain collapse? Opportunity_cost_reading's timeline critique depends on large-reactor data; SMR track record is zero.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + deferred axis construction_timeline_lock_in

omegas.description: China is deploying nuclear at 6-8 GW/year. Does this invalidate opportunity_cost_reading's deployment-rate claim, or does it confirm systems_transition_reading's centralized-state prerequisite? Western liberal democracies have not matched this rate.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) — model trained primarily on Western energy-policy discourse

omegas.description: Do portfolio_optimization and opportunity_cost readings collapse if both accept 'maximize carbon reduction per dollar per year' as the shared metric? Current separation depends on portfolio reading treating reliability as non-fungible with cost, but both could converge on cost-effectiveness if storage costs drop.
omegas.source: §1.3-K coherence check — readings may not remain distinct under all future conditions

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: grid_intermittency_constraint classified as mountain (physical limit) but storage technology trajectory may reclassify it as rope (coordination problem) or piton (policy choice to under-invest in storage). Generated omega_storage_breakthrough to bound this uncertainty. Also: construction_timeline_lock_in deferred as mountain but SMR claims (unproven) could collapse it; omega_smr_deployment documents this.
